lastCompletedStory.title: CRITICAL: The false-positive class US-R1-001 was written to close is still OPEN…

nextStoryContext: US-R2-001 closed the round-2 CRITICAL: argv shape + cwd (US-R1-001's absolute-argv[0] anchor on isSidecarArgv) was proven, live against the real production path, to still misclassify an unrelated process as this project's sidecar -- Bun.spawn(['/usr/bin/tail','-F','sidecar'], {cwd}) still yielded fallbackSidecarKilled=true and killFn received the tail's pid (round 1's own recorded repro, unfixed by round 1's diff). Root cause: argv shape alone can never distinguish a real self-spawn from an unrelated tool invocation that happens to end in the literal token 'sidecar' with an absolute argv[0] and a matching cwd -- 'sidecar' is a routine grep/test-filter term in this very repo. Fix: added a process-IDENTITY check on top of argv+cwd. The real sidecar process always holds `.claude/cam-supervisor.log` open on fd 1/2 for its entire lifetime (spawnSidecarDefault, src/commands/run.ts, redirects stdio there via `openSync(logPath, 'a')`); an unrelated process cannot hold this project's own log file open by accident. `defaultListProcesses` (src/commands/stop.ts) now runs a single `lsof -p <pid> -F fn` per candidate (same call count as before, just unrestricted instead of `-a -d cwd` scoped) and parses BOTH the cwd (fd 'cwd') AND every other open file descriptor from that one call; a candidate is only ever returned once it holds `<cwd>/.claude/cam-supervisor.log` open as one of its fds. Added a shared `SIDECAR_LOG_FILENAME` constant (src/supervisor/sidecar-pid.ts) so `run.ts` (the writer/spawner) and `stop.ts` (the reader/verifier) never drift on the literal filename. `matchesSidecarForProject`/`isSidecarArgv` are UNCHANGED in signature and remain argv+cwd only (their existing unit tests, which inject hand-built ProcessRecords, are unaffected by design -- the new check lives one layer up, inside `defaultListProcesses`, which is production-only and only exercised for real via the real-process integration test). Rewrote test/integration/stop-defaultlistprocesses-real.test.ts (US-R1-003's real-I/O test) to spawn THREE concurrent real processes in one private mkdtemp cwd: (1) a genuine sidecar-shaped process that ALSO holds a real cam-supervisor.log open via stdio redirection -- must be matched + SIGTERM'd; (2) a sidecar-shaped DECOY with identical argv+cwd but no log held open -- reproduces the exact round-1/round-2 CRITICAL class, must survive; (3) the pre-existing adjacent non-sidecar-argv process -- must survive (quick filter). All three assertions pass against real ps+lsof+SIGTERM, no fakes. Additionally hand-verified the literal round-1/round-2 repro command (`Bun.spawn(['/usr/bin/tail','-F','sidecar'], {cwd})`) directly against `performStop` in a throwaway script: fallbackSidecarKilled is now `false`, killCalls is `[]`. Empirically verified (not just documented) the underlying lsof -F fn field-pairing assumption (f<fd> line immediately followed by n<name> line) on this macOS/BSD lsof by spawning a real tail process both with and without stdio redirected to a literal cam-supervisor.log path and inspecting raw `lsof -p <pid> -F fn` output before writing the parser. File-size ceilings raised for the three files this story grew (src/commands/stop.ts 733->789, src/commands/run.ts 1221->1222, src/supervisor/sidecar-pid.ts 230->240) per the established _ref dated-note convention; no other budgeted file touched. Full quality spine green: typecheck 0 errors, 5934 tests pass (0 fail), check:all (lint/file-size/debt-markers/version-skips/coverage/dead-code/dup/ci-parity/agents-md/test-sleeps/skip-ratchet) all ok. This closes the last known round-2 CRITICAL for CAM-482; scripts/cam/prd.json shows a pre-existing unstaged modification from before this story started (not authored by this story, left untouched per 'the implementer does not edit prd.json'/'supervisor is sole writer of passes') -- the next agent may want to inspect it for its own context before assuming a clean baseline.

officialDocsValidated.summary: The Linux man page confirms the field-letter semantics this fix relies on (p=PID, f=file-descriptor id, n=file name), matching the implementation. It does not document line-ordering/pairing (whether an 'n' line always immediately follows its owning 'f' line), and this is a Linux doc while the actual runtime target here is macOS/BSD lsof (a related but distinct implementation). Docs alone were insufficient to trust the parser's ordering assumption, so it was additionally verified empirically against the real macOS lsof binary (spawned real processes with known open files, inspected raw `lsof -p <pid> -F fn` output) before writing parseLsofOpenFiles -- this empirical probe, not the man page, is the actual evidence of record for the parser's correctness; the man page only corroborates the field-letter meanings.
